description: Implement the jobs runtime module (src/doot/jobs.nim) with SQLite-backed job queue, worker pool, scheduler, enqueue/dispatch, retry logic, and stuck job detection. Also add AST nodes and parser support for job/schedule/enqueue syntax.
steps: 1. Add new AST node kinds to src/doot/ast.nim: nkJob (jobName: string, jobParam: string, jobBody: seq[DootNode]), nkSchedule (scheduleName: string, scheduleInterval: string, scheduleBody: seq[DootNode]), nkEnqueue (enqueueName: DootNode, enqueueArgs: seq[KeyValuePair]). Add constructor procs following existing patterns.

2. Update src/doot/parser.nim: In parseApp(), add cases for tkJob -> parseJob() and tkSchedule -> parseSchedule(). In parseHandlerBody(), add case for tkJob -> parseEnqueueStatement() (since enqueue is an identifier, handle 'enqueue' in parseStatementStartingWithIdent or add a new token). Implement parseJob() to parse: job "name" do |payload| ... end. Implement parseSchedule() to parse: schedule "name", every: "interval" do ... end. For enqueue, handle it as an identifier-started statement in parseStatementStartingWithIdent - when identifier is 'enqueue', parse: enqueue "job_name", key: value, key: value.

3. Create src/doot/jobs.nim with the following components: (a) JobsTableSQL constant with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _doot_jobs schema matching the spec (id, job_type, payload, status, run_at, attempts, locked_at, error, created_at, updated_at) plus indexes on status and run_at. (b) Types: JobStatus enum (jsPending, jsRunning, jsCompleted, jsFailed), JobRecord object, JobHandler proc type (proc(payload: JsonNode): Future[void]), WorkerPool ref object, ScheduleEntry object. (c) Interval parsing: proc parseInterval(s: string): Duration that handles '30 seconds', '5 minutes', '1 hour', '1 day', '1 week'. (d) Job queue operations: initJobsTable(db), enqueueJob(db, jobType, payload, runAt, delay), claimNextJob(db, lockTimeout), completeJob(db, jobId), failJob(db, jobId, error, maxAttempts), retryJob(db, jobId), unlockStuckJobs(db, timeout). (e) Worker pool: newWorkerPool(db, poolSize, pollInterval), registerJobHandler(pool, jobType, handler), startWorkerPool(pool) as async, stopWorkerPool(pool). (f) Scheduler: addSchedule(pool, name, interval, handler), startScheduler(pool) as async. (g) Job status queries: getJobCounts(db), getFailedJobs(db), getRecentJobs(db, limit).

4. The worker pool polling loop: each worker is an async proc that loops: poll for pending job where run_at <= now and status = 'pending', claim it (UPDATE set locked_at and status = 'running'), execute the registered handler, on success call completeJob, on failure call failJob. Poll interval configurable (default 5 seconds for tests, 10-30 seconds for production). Use asyncdispatch sleepAsync between polls.

5. The scheduler loop: an async proc that checks each registered schedule entry, if enough time has passed since last insertion, inserts a new job into the queue. The worker pool then picks it up normally.

6. Stuck job detection: unlockStuckJobs(db, timeout: Duration) finds jobs where status = 'running' and locked_at < now - timeout, resets them to status = 'pending' and clears locked_at. Called periodically by the worker pool.

7. Retry logic: when a job fails, if attempts < maxAttempts (default 3), set status back to 'pending' (re-enqueue). If attempts >= maxAttempts, set status to 'failed'. The failJob proc handles this logic.
acceptance_criteria: src/doot/ast.nim compiles with new nkJob, nkSchedule, nkEnqueue node kinds
src/doot/parser.nim correctly parses 'job "name" do |payload| ... end' into nkJob AST node
src/doot/parser.nim correctly parses 'schedule "name", every: "1 hour" do ... end' into nkSchedule AST node
Parser handles 'enqueue "job_name", key: value' as a statement in handler bodies
src/doot/jobs.nim compiles and exports all required types and procs
initJobsTable creates _doot_jobs table with correct schema and indexes
enqueueJob inserts a row with correct fields (job_type, payload as JSON, status=pending, run_at)
claimNextJob atomically selects and locks a pending job
Worker pool picks up and executes enqueued jobs
Failed jobs have status='failed' and attempts incremented
Stuck job detection unlocks jobs with locked_at exceeding timeout
Scheduler inserts jobs at configured intervals
parseInterval correctly parses '30 seconds', '5 minutes', '1 hour', '1 day'

findings: 1. JobHandler type uses {.closure.} pragma (no gcsafe) since SQLite is single-threaded. 2. Async exception handling requires yield+fut.failed pattern instead of try/except around await. 3. Worker pool uses std/options for claimNextJob return type. 4. All 44 tests pass including parser tests for job/schedule/enqueue syntax.
